title: Postgraduate Courses in Music
transcript:
Speaker 0: Section three. You will hear two students, Anna and Chris, talking about postgraduate courses in music. First, you have some time to look at questions 21 to 25. Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25.
Speaker 1: Hi, Chris. What are you doing here? I thought you were supposed to be revising for your finals in the library.
Speaker 2: Yeah. Well, I decided it was time for a break. I really wasn't being very productive, so thought I'd come and have a coffee and some fresh air to see if that'd help. Oh, what are you doing with all those prospectuses?
Speaker 1: Well, I'm trying to decide which university to apply to for my MA in music. The choice is really overwhelming.
Speaker 2: Well, that certainly is a big pile of prospectuses. Maybe talking about it will help you at least narrow it down. I've got some time, and to be honest, it'll be a welcome distraction from my dissertation.
Speaker 1: Great. Thanks, Chris. So far, the universities that appeal the most are the Academy in London, Leeds Conservatory of Contemporary Music, and the Henry Music Institute, which is also in London.
Speaker 2: I'm not an expert, but wouldn't the Henry Music Institute be the best as it's the one that everyone's heard of?
Speaker 1: Well, yes and no. Leeds Conservatory of Contemporary Music is also pretty famous. And although the academy in London is less well known, they've got some excellent modules on offer.
Speaker 2: But still, it's always good to have a well known name on your CV, even if Leeds Conservatory of Contemporary Music and the Academy in London are good. What about the entry requirements? That might help you to make a decision.
Speaker 1: Well, funny you should say that, because I was just looking at them. The Academy in London requires an audition, as does the Henry Music Institute.
Speaker 2: Leeds Conservatory of Contemporary Music doesn't?
Speaker 1: No. They want candidates to compose a piece of music instead before attending an interview.
Speaker 2: Don't the others require you to do that? Compose, that is.
Speaker 1: No. The others ask you to write an assignment stating why you want to join the course first of all. But if I pass that stage, then I'll also have to attend a face to face interview like the other two places with the head of school. Assuming that goes okay, then I'll be accepted onto the course. Right.
Speaker 2: Sounds tough.
Speaker 1: I know. But I suppose it's for a master's degree, so I wasn't expecting it to be easy.
Speaker 2: What about the fees? Are they all the same?
Speaker 1: Well, surprisingly, the fee structures are very different.
Speaker 2: Why is that?
Speaker 1: I really don't know. But, for example, the Henry Music Institute is the most expensive at £8,000 a year. Next comes the Academy in London, and the cheapest is Leeds Conservatory of Contemporary Music.
Speaker 2: How much are they exactly?
Speaker 1: Well, for a full time course lasting one year, it's £7,000 at the Academy in London and £6,000 at Leeds Conservatory of Contemporary Music.
Speaker 2: Okay. Well, what other expenses do you have to take into consideration, like train fares, for example? If you're going to be travelling home and back during the holidays, that's got to be a factor.
Speaker 1: I'm not worried about that. Though insurance is an added cost, as I'll need to make sure my instrument is covered. However, all of them require me to send in a check for the charges for applying before they'll process my application.
Speaker 2: Is that normal?
Speaker 1: Apparently.
Speaker 2: Can I have a look?
Speaker 1: Yes, of course. Here you are. What is it?
Speaker 2: Well, I think you might have a problem.
Speaker 1: Why? What is it?
Speaker 2: Well, it says here that the deadline is January 9. That's next week.
Speaker 1: Where? Let me see. Oh, you're right. Which prospectus is this?
Speaker 2: The Henry Music Institute.
Speaker 1: Oh, no. What am I going to do?
Speaker 2: Make your decision now.
Speaker 1: Is the closing date the same for all of them?
Speaker 2: Let's check. Look here. Leeds Conservatory of Contemporary Music is on the nineteenth, but the academy in London isn't until the thirtieth of this month.
Speaker 1: Okay. I'd better hurry up and make a decision.
Speaker 0: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 26 to 30. Now listen and answer questions 26 to 30.
Speaker 1: Right. Now apart from those three colleges, I also wanted to have a quick flick through Northdowne Colleges and the one from the James Academy of Music.
Speaker 2: Look. Here it is. Facilities at Northdowne College.
Speaker 1: What does it say?
Speaker 2: Well, it has a library with a dedicated historical research section that's world famous.
Speaker 1: That's all very interesting, but it's not going to make me go there.
Speaker 2: Okay. The Academy in London has four campuses all around Central London. They all have large common rooms, and there's one twenty four hour cafeteria at the biggest site.
Speaker 1: That's nice. But for me, the most important thing is somewhere to practice.
Speaker 2: Yes. Of course.
Speaker 1: Right. Now where did I see it? Okay. Here it is. Look. Now this is good.
Speaker 2: Mhmm.
Speaker 1: Leeds Conservatory of Contemporary Music has over 100 teaching and practice studios. What a luxury. Here, there are only 10, and it's really difficult to find one empty. So I often have to play in the gardens.
Speaker 2: Oh, dear.
Speaker 1: Anyway, that's the past, and this place looks great.
Speaker 2: Well, what about the Henry Music Institute? Look. There's a new suite with the latest that technology has to offer Mhmm. And a small museum dedicated to the history of music. That's really impressive.
Speaker 1: I don't think I'm really that interested in using computers while making music. So that's not a selling point, really. But look, this place is interesting, the James Academy of Music. It comes recommended by lots of people in the music industry, and all of its courses have a business element, as well as having a professional studio for recording albums.
Speaker 2: Wow. That sounds really cutting edge. So are you any closer to making a decision now?
Speaker 0: That is the end of section three. You now have half a minute to check your answers.
